key_insight: Orthogonalized momentum can fail on nonsmooth convex optimization when momentum is fixed, but becomes reliable when momentum is adaptive and paired with vanishing step sizes.
engineering_relevance: For matrix-valued optimization in deep learning, the paper shows when Muon-style updates are unsafe and proposes MAGD as a practical, dimension-aware alternative with convergence guarantees.
method: Proves a failure case for Muon on locally Lipschitz convex objectives with fixed momentum.
Shows asymptotic convergence can be recovered with adaptive momentum approaching 1 and vanishing step sizes.
Introduces MAGD, which blends orthogonalized momentum with gradient information weighted by relative progress.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence and lower-bound results, plus experiments on synthetic problems, image classification, and LLM pretraining.
watch_item: The guarantees depend on bounded iterates and regularity assumptions, so performance may be sensitive to step-size and momentum scheduling in practice.
